title: The indexed-retrieval fallback warning names no cause
description:
When indexed retrieval fails under the default `auto` policy, retrieval.ts falls back to the reference backend and warns:

  native indexed retrieval failed; using the in-memory reference backend

That is the SAME sentence for every cause -- a corrupt edge record, an unreadable generation, a native version mismatch, a permissions problem. A user who sees it cannot act on it, and a maintainer cannot triage it without attaching a debugger and re-running with `policy: 'indexed'` to see the real throw. LCLI-497 took exactly that route.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT THE FIX. Interpolating the cause -- `deriveMessage(cause)` -- would carry internal vocabulary into public output: the LCLI-497 cause reads 'Ladybug projection verification failed: indexed edge is invalid'. test/indexed-retrieval.test.ts asserts that public stdout and stderr match none of /MATCH \(|recordKey|projection\.lbdb|ladybug|databasePath|sourceFingerprint/i, and that invariant is deliberate: the storage engine is an implementation detail, not part of the CLI contract.

So this needs a SANITISED diagnosis: a small closed set of fallback reasons that name what went wrong in the CLI's own vocabulary ('the indexed snapshot disagrees with the exported records', 'the indexed generation could not be opened', 'the native driver version is not supported') mapped from the cause, rather than the cause's own text. A closed set is also testable, which a free-form interpolation is not.

Out of scope for LCLI-497, which is a release blocker and should stay five lines plus its regression tests.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The auto-policy fallback warning distinguishes at least the verification, generation-open, and unsupported-driver causes
Every emitted reason is drawn from a closed set defined in one place, not interpolated from the underlying error text
The existing assertion that public output carries no native identifiers, paths, or Cypher still holds for every reason in that set
A test asserts the reason for at least one real failure, not only that some warning appeared

references: LCLI-497 (the defect that needed this diagnosis and did not have it)
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #81, CI run 34921602022 on head c94088bc -- all checks SUCCESS or SKIPPED, none failed. That run validates the implementation; the closing commit adds tracker records only.

AC1 -- the advisory distinguishes verification, generation-open and unsupported-driver causes.
Six reasons, and the set covers more than the three named: `unsupported-platform`, `driver-unavailable`, `verification-failed`, `generation-unavailable`, `preflight-failed`, `unexpected`. `preflight-failed` exists because "we never reached the native boundary" is a different fact from "we did and it went wrong", and no property of the error can tell you which; `unexpected` exists because a closed set with no residual bucket forces a wrong classification rather than admitting one.

AC2 -- every reason is drawn from a closed set in one place, not interpolated.
`REFERENCE_FALLBACK_REASONS` and `referenceFallbackMessage` in retrieval.ts. Workspace retrieval DERIVES its sentence from the same function rather than restating it, so a reason added in one place cannot go missing in the other -- the two vocabularies differ by one word and would otherwise drift.

Closed rather than interpolated for two reasons, and both are load-bearing. The underlying cause reads "Ladybug projection verification failed: ...", and the storage engine is an implementation detail this CLI does not expose. And an interpolation is not testable: a caller can assert that a reason IS `verification-failed`, and can assert nothing useful about a sentence free to change with any internal message.

AC3 -- the no-native-identifiers assertion still holds for every reason.
Asserted over the WHOLE set rather than over whichever reason a test happened to trigger, using the same pattern the existing public-output test uses. The same test also asserts the six sentences are distinct, which a set of identical strings would not be -- the defect being fixed would otherwise pass an existence check.

AC4 -- a test asserts the reason for a real failure.
Four of the six are driven by real failures: a real native loader throw (`driver-unavailable`), a real source preflight failure (`preflight-failed`), the Windows platform path (`unsupported-platform`), and a real contended writer lock with no matching generation (`generation-unavailable`). The preflight case additionally asserts it is NOT reported as the driver reason, which is the distinction that did not exist before.

`verification-failed` is staged with an injected reader, and the test says why rather than hiding it: the lifecycle QUARANTINES AND REBUILDS tampered bytes before a read can fail on them -- proven by the adjacent test that does corrupt a real generation and gets a recovery -- so corruption on disk produces a rebuild, not a verification failure. The staged error is constructed from the same exported marker the driver's own `corrupt()` uses, so the two cannot drift apart.

BEYOND THE CRITERIA, AND THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF. The route taken when no indexed generation exists fell back with NO advisory at all. So empty stderr was consistent with both "indexed ran" and "fell back silently", and a signal that fires on some routes and not others is worse than one that never fires -- it invites the inference that it is total. Every route now announces itself.

opum-agent left that explicitly as this repository's call and leaned toward warning; the reasoning for doing it here rather than filing it again is that "the advisory names its cause" and "the advisory is emitted" are the same defect from two angles, and fixing one without the other ships a warning that names its cause except when there is none. The finding itself came from opum-cli-e2e asking what its own stderr assertion could prove and going back to lore's source rather than defending the row.

It is a behaviour change to two previously-quiet paths, so two existing tests -- both named for exactly those paths -- now assert the advisory instead of expecting stderr parity with the reference loader. Their payload assertions are untouched.

VERIFICATION FAILURES ARE CLASSIFIED FROM A DECLARED MARKER, not a message match. A proxy that happens to correlate with the thing you mean is not the thing you mean; that is LCLI-497's lesson applied one layer up, deliberately. The marker lives in `ladybug-source` rather than `ladybug-driver` so `retrieval.ts` can read it without importing the native boundary it is careful not to touch, and its value says "indexed" rather than the engine's name because it reaches public output in the error envelope.

Mutation-tested: collapsing every reason to one sentence fails 3; silencing the generation-unavailable route again fails 2; classifying by message text instead of the marker fails 1.

Validation: bun test 3048 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; typecheck clean; lint clean; lore check 78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
